branch_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Citizens to Register and Report Urban Issues
branch_001.rationale: The initial goals (llg_001, llg_002, llg_003) focus on establishing and personalizing a citizen's account, which is a prerequisite for participating in the system. The subsequent goals (llg_004, llg_005, llg_006, llg_007) detail the process of submitting comprehensive reports about urban issues. Together, these operations form a complete flow for citizens to engage with a platform designed for reporting community problems.

branch_002.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports
branch_002.rationale: The low-level goals collectively aim to provide citizens with comprehensive tools to track the status and history of their submitted reports, receive timely updates, and control their notification preferences. This ensures citizens are well-informed and have agency over their interactions with the reporting system.

branch_003.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the functionalities required for a citizen to engage in a two-way communication with a municipal operator concerning a specific report, including sending messages, receiving responses, and reviewing the entire conversation history. This ensures effective and transparent interaction for report resolution.

branch_004.rationale: Both low-level goals directly contribute to the overarching objective of allowing citizens to submit reports without their identity being publicly disclosed. One goal focuses on the user's ability to choose this option, and the other focuses on the system's responsibility to enforce it, ensuring the anonymity is maintained.

branch_005.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Citizens to Access and Monitor Public Reports
branch_005.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe functionalities that allow citizens to discover (view, filter) and track (subscribe, unsubscribe) publicly available reports submitted by other citizens. These operations are all geared towards providing citizens with the means to stay informed about and engage with community-reported information.

branch_006.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Non-Registered Users to Access and View Public Reports
branch_006.rationale: All low-level goals describe actions by a non-registered user to retrieve, display, and filter public reports using various interfaces and methods. They collectively contribute to the overarching goal of making public reports accessible and viewable to non-registered users.

branch_007.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide Public Access to Reporting Statistics
branch_007.rationale: Both low-level goals describe functionalities for non-registered users to view different types of statistics related to reports. One focuses on categorical breakdowns, and the other on temporal trends, but both contribute to the overarching goal of making reporting data publicly accessible for informational purposes.

branch_008.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the essential steps for office staff to perform an initial review of reports. This includes identifying reports awaiting review, accessing their full details, and documenting internal observations during the review process.

branch_009.rationale: These operations collectively describe the process by which office staff evaluate citizen reports and make a formal decision regarding their acceptance or rejection, including providing necessary justifications for rejections. They all contribute to the initial handling and disposition of incoming reports.

branch_010.rationale: These low-level goals collectively define the various states a report can assume throughout its lifecycle, from initial submission to different stages of processing and eventual outcomes. They describe how the report's status is set and updated, either automatically by the system or manually by office staff, to reflect its current position in the workflow.

branch_011.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the process of identifying approved reports that require assignment, performing the actual assignment to either internal departments or external personnel/companies, and receiving system support for making informed assignment decisions. They all contribute to the overarching objective of ensuring that approved reports are efficiently and correctly directed to the appropriate entities for further action.

branch_012.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Technical Office Staff to Monitor Report Progress
branch_012.rationale: These operations collectively provide the technical office staff with comprehensive capabilities to view, track, and report on the current status, historical changes, and overall progress of reports and issues assigned to their office. They all contribute to effective oversight and information retrieval regarding report lifecycle management.

branch_013.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the essential steps for technical office staff to track the progress and document the outcome of work performed on a report, from the initiation of active work to its successful completion and the detailed recording of how it was resolved. They all contribute to effectively managing the lifecycle of a report's resolution.

branch_014.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage communication with external maintenance personnel regarding assigned reports
branch_014.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete lifecycle of communication between technical office staff and external maintenance personnel concerning a specific report: sending messages, receiving responses, and reviewing the entire interaction history. These operations are all integral to effectively managing and tracking communication related to assigned reports.

branch_015.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage Assigned Reports for External Maintenance Personnel
branch_015.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the essential steps an external maintenance personnel takes to identify, understand, and formally accept responsibility for reports assigned to them. These operations are all part of the initial phase of managing an assigned report, from discovery to formal acknowledgment.

branch_016.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Facilitate External Maintenance Personnel Reporting of Work Progress and Completion
branch_016.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the essential actions for external maintenance personnel to report the lifecycle of their assigned tasks. They cover initiating work, marking it as finished, and providing necessary evidence, all contributing to a comprehensive reporting process for maintenance activities.

branch_017.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable External Maintenance Personnel to Communicate with the Municipal Technical Office regarding Reports
branch_017.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the essential functionalities for external maintenance personnel to engage in two-way communication (sending and receiving messages) and maintain an auditable record (viewing history) with the municipal technical office concerning specific reports. They all contribute to establishing and managing this communication channel.

branch_018.rationale: All low-level goals describe various administrative tasks performed by a municipal administrator to set up, customize, and maintain the operational parameters, user access, data structures, and external interfaces of the system. They collectively aim to ensure the system functions according to municipal policies and integrates effectively.

branch_019.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Municipal Administrator to Monitor and Analyze System Performance and Usage
branch_019.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe various methods for the municipal administrator to access, customize, visualize, and export statistical data and reports. These operations are all geared towards providing the administrator with the necessary tools to monitor system performance, understand user interactions, evaluate system health, and conduct in-depth analysis of operational data.

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Submit Urban Issue Reports' is supported by the documentation and represents a distinct, independently satisfiable stakeholder outcome for the Citizen actor. While the bottom-up reconstruction suggests including 'Register', registration is a prerequisite for the account lifecycle rather than the core functional outcome of reporting. The sibling goal 'Maintain Report Anonymity' is a specific attribute/option within the submission process, not a separate end-to-end outcome that would make 'Submit' redundant. The goal is correctly scoped to the act of reporting issues, which is the primary value proposition for the citizen in this context. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs contain a material defect because llg_003 ('UploadCitizenProfilePhoto') is unsupported by the documentation in the context of the parent goal 'Submit Urban Issue Reports'. While the documentation mentions that users can upload a personal photo in the 'user settings panel' (Section C), this is a profile management feature, not a prerequisite or component of the act of submitting an urban issue report. Including it under this HLG conflates account profile customization with the core reporting workflow. Additionally, the parent goal 'Submit Urban Issue Reports' implies the complete process of creating a report, which includes the mandatory selection of the anonymity option (Section A: 'the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous'). Although there is a sibling HLG 'Maintain Report Anonymity', the act of *selecting* this option is part of the submission form flow. However, the most critical error is the inclusion of the profile photo upload, which is unrelated to the submission act. The registration steps (llg_001, llg_002) are prerequisites, which is acceptable in a bottom-up decomposition if the HLG is interpreted as 'Enable Citizen to Submit', but strictly speaking, 'Submit' is the action. Given the strict instruction to audit every LLG for support in the parent context, llg_003 is clearly out of scope for 'Submit Urban Issue Reports'.

The documentation describes a broader capability for citizens to 'follow' their reports, which includes receiving notifications, viewing status changes, and communicating with operators. The sibling goal 'Communicate with Administration' covers the messaging aspect, but 'Receive Report Updates' only covers the notification/status aspect. More importantly, the bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports' suggests a broader intention. However, looking at the existing HLGs, 'Monitor Community Issues' covers following *other* reports. The goal of tracking *one's own* reports is distinct. The original goal 'Receive Report Updates' is a valid, independently satisfiable stakeholder outcome (staying informed about one's own specific reports). It is not redundant with 'Communicate with Administration' (which is about two-way messaging) or 'Monitor Community Issues' (which is about others' reports). The granularity is appropriate for a high-level goal in this context, as it represents a distinct value proposition (transparency/trust for the reporter). The reconstruction 'Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports' is broader and might encompass communication, but since 'Communicate with Administration' is a separate HLG, 'Receive Report Updates' remains a distinct, supported, and appropriately scoped goal for the passive receipt of status information. It is not a mere workflow step but a key feature for citizen engagement. Therefore, it should be kept. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs contain a material defect. LLG 'llg_004' (ViewReportHistoryLog) is unsupported by the documentation. The text describes receiving notifications on state changes and viewing the current status, but does not mention a chronological log of all actions or updates for the citizen to view. Additionally, the parent goal 'Receive Report Updates' is not fully covered. The documentation explicitly states that 'municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply.' While there is a sibling HLG 'Communicate with Administration', the specific capability of *receiving* these operator-initiated messages as part of the 'updates' flow is distinct from the citizen-initiated communication often implied by 'Communicate'. However, looking closely at the sibling 'Communicate with Administration', it covers 'exchange messages'. The prompt asks to audit against the parent 'Receive Report Updates'. The documentation says: 'First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification... Furthermore, municipal operators... can send the reporting citizen a message... Each time the citizen receives a notification... they also get an email'. The current LLGs cover status retrieval (llg_002), push notifications (llg_003), and disabling emails (llg_001). They miss the capability to *receive* messages from operators (which are distinct from status change notifications) and potentially the *email* notification itself (llg_001 is about disabling, not receiving). More critically, llg_004 is an invention. The documentation does not support a 'history log' view for citizens. It supports viewing the report page (which shows description) and receiving notifications. It does not explicitly state a chronological log of *all* updates is visible to the citizen, only that they receive notifications. Therefore, llg_004 is unsupported. Also, the capability to receive email notifications (the default behavior) is not explicitly an LLG, only the disabling of it. However, the most glaring error is llg_004. Another potential issue: The documentation says 'citizen can receive updates... through various channels... notification on the platform... email'. LLG 003 covers platform notification. LLG 001 covers disabling email. There is no LLG for 'Receive Email Notification'. Is this essential? Yes, it's a primary channel. But often 'Receive Notification' implies the mechanism. Let's look at llg_004 again. 'ViewReportHistoryLog' is definitely not in the text. The text says 'Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.' It doesn't mention a history log. So llg_004 is unsupported. Missing capability: Receiving email notifications (distinct from disabling them).

LLG_001 (Browse) and LLG_002 (Filter) correspond to viewing the summary table/map. LLG_003 (Follow) and LLG_004 (Unfollow) correspond to the ability to subscribe/unsubscribe to notifications for other reports. replacement_request.generation_project_description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: [https://iris.sad.ve.it/](https://iris.sad.ve.it/?utm_source=gemini). The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal [https://developers.italia.it/](https://developers.italia.it/?utm_source=gemini).

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section).
If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:

* Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved.
Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
* Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo).
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The project description outlines functional requirements for citizens (reporting, updates, communication, anonymity, monitoring), non-registered users (public view, public stats), organization office staff (review, approve/reject, workflow), technical office staff (assignment, tracking, status updates, internal communication), external maintenance personnel (task receipt, status updates, communication), and municipal administrators (configuration, private statistics). All these responsibilities are explicitly covered by the current High-Level Goals. Specifically, the 'Access Comprehensive Statistics' HLG for the Municipal Administrator covers the requirement to view private statistics (charts and tables) in addition to public ones. No other actor-level functional responsibilities are left uncovered.
